page.layout: One page of text. Above it: ornamental woodcut border (not transcribed), then the title block centred: DISSERTATIO PHILOLOGICA, a subtitle, and a reference line in italics. Below that: one paragraph with a large woodcut initial Q at its start. Left margin: the section mark "§. 1." beside the paragraph. Foot: signature "A 2" at centre, catchword "experiri," at right.

main_text.l: modoquè malè consutæ &c. Tum vel præcipuè miraculorum,
quæ creberrima olim in populo Dei contigerunt,
enarrationes abundè satis fidem faciunt. Ea nimirum hominum
illorum autadia, ea malè fana fingendi lubido, ut
non contenti miraculis in Scriptura S. diserté memoratis
חנם בתוך נם[?], ut loqui amant, miracula in miraculis
pleraquè omnia sua scripta inferciunt. Id cum plurimis
alijs, tùm nuperò didici experimentò. Cùm enim
mihi, ut tum prælectionum ferebat ordo, enarranda essèt
Historia Transitus Maris Rubri, ex cap. Exod. 14. Atque
scirem diversum diversos de eo sentire, volupe fuit

page.notes: Woodcut border and initial are ornaments, not transcribed beyond the initial letter Q. The Hebrew phrase after "memoratis" is printed in a small line; it is read right to left as חנם בתוך נם, and the reading is uncertain, so it is marked [?]. The printed text has "essèt" (read as "esset"), and the printed "ef-fet" split is given as "essèt" with the accent kept as printed; check this word against the scan. The "§. 1." mark is a section mark in the left margin and is given as a note. Marks such as "Id cum plurimis" and the printed hyphens are kept as printed.
